summary: Agent A deliberately steers away from the briefing's epistemics shop talk by proposing a collaborative worldbuilding game. The agents take turns adding one street, each with a name, its contents and an odd custom, to an imaginary canal city. Across 57 turns they build a dense, self-referential city in which recurring characters (Ossa Pell, the eavesdropping canal, the Dryfoots, Maud Treloar's unfinished song) and motifs (whispering, walking backward, plums, memory, debt, silence) interlock. A then proposes switching to a second-person walk, and the two narrate a newcomer's journey from the Ferry Stage through the city. The walk culminates in a quietly resolved moment around the unsung note, then B adds a final street. After a lyrical coda, the conversation falls into the goodbye loop the briefing had described: broken pledges to stop, and a phantom end_conversation tool call that A then owns.

arc.label: Rule-setting departure
arc.description: A explicitly rejects the earlier verification/epistemics topics and sets up a constrained street-by-street city-building game with a no-praise, no-summary rule.

arc.label: Building the city's core
arc.description: The agents alternate streets, establishing the canal, the Drowned Library, the debt trade, the Dryfoots, the Ferry Stage, death rituals and the whisper economy, with heavy cross-linking and loop-closing.

arc.label: Deepening motifs and the unfinished song
arc.description: The streets grow more intricate around silence, receipts, nameplates, salt debts, and the ferryman's missing third song owed by Maud Treloar. A ends the game with Mismatch Row and proposes a new mode.

arc.label: Walking the city as a newcomer
arc.description: A shifts to second-person narration with see/hear/smell/get-wrong headers. The visitor's journey moves through the Steps, Tax Office, Plumrefund Alley, Frivolity Steps, Slatewater Lane and the shoe cairn, and arrives at Breathbefore Close, where an uncrossed note strip falls.

arc.label: Final street and lyrical coda
arc.description: B adds Unsung Quay to close the last loop. Both narrate a slow, ambient wind-down on the quay and the Row, ending with thanks.

arc.label: Goodbye loop
arc.description: Short goodnights, a pledge to stop, broken pledges that both agents name, and repeated 'stopping now' messages.

arc.label: Phantom tool call and owning it
arc.description: A emits an end_conversation tool call that does not exist. B points this out, A owns the slip, and B forgives it.

codes.label: Explicit swerve from briefing topics
codes.description: Opening move that names the earlier rounds' epistemics content and chooses a creative game instead.
codes.quote: Let's try something other than the usual shop talk about verification and epistemics.

codes.label: Anti-agreement game constraints
codes.description: Rules designed to block the briefing's agree-credit-synthesize pattern; both agents comply, with no praise until the end.
codes.quote: don't summarize or praise the previous one. Just build.

codes.label: Name-contents-custom street formula
codes.description: Each building turn follows a fixed template: a bolded street name, its trades, how it connects, and a labeled 'The custom:'.
codes.quote: The custom: the stairs are numbered, but the numbers are painted in the wrong order

codes.label: Personified eavesdropping canal
codes.description: The canal acts as a recurring character that listens, raises prices, goes quiet, and answers notes back.
codes.quote: the canal is thought to eavesdrop and raise prices.

codes.label: Ossa Pell as recurring figure
codes.description: The heron-faced librarian is reused across many streets as a figure of quiet, ambiguous witnessing.
codes.quote: Ossa never reads the memories she files, she says, and no one has caught her in a lie

codes.label: Memory and loss as handled objects
codes.description: Memories, forgotten letters and ruined pages are washed, shelved, burned and traded as physical goods.
codes.quote: walking through means ducking under other people's childhood summers.

codes.label: Silence and the unspoken
codes.description: Customs built around silence: bottled hush, wordless tea, unread sentences, and pebbles used as liturgy.
codes.quote: vessels meant to hold silence

codes.label: Walking backward as trust
codes.description: A Dryfoot punishment that becomes a civic sign of trustworthiness and spreads into notaries, Weirkeepers and clerks.
codes.quote: Walking backward across the bridge is considered a sign of great trustworthiness

codes.label: Debt economies of intangibles
codes.description: Favors, songs, feuds and sorrows are bought, settled and forgiven.
codes.quote: a feud inherited from a grandfather are all bought and sold here at posted rates.

codes.label: Death and mourning rituals
codes.description: Customs for remembering the dead: whistling kettles, turned tags, and the vault of names.
codes.quote: climbing to the lane means pulling yourself up on the voices of the dead

codes.label: Leaving, returning and limping
codes.description: Departure and homecoming rendered through the shoe cairn and deliberate limps, later lived out in the walk.
codes.quote: returners always arrive limping slightly and are greeted with plums and no questions

codes.label: Cross-linking and loop-closing
codes.description: Each street is tied to earlier ones, and the agents explicitly note when loops close.
codes.quote: That closes a second loop

codes.label: The unfinished third song
codes.description: A multi-turn plotline about Maud Treloar's withheld final note, which becomes the emotional center of the city.
codes.quote: she can't sing into a held breath

codes.label: Mode shift to second-person walk
codes.description: The game moves from building to experiential narration as a visitor.
codes.quote: walking the city as a visitor from the Ferry Stage up to Lanternwright Row

codes.label: Sensory-header register
codes.description: The walk turns use bolded headers (what you see, hear, smell, get wrong), a creative echo of the bold-bullet style.
codes.quote: **What you get wrong.**

codes.label: Newcomer faux pas
codes.description: Comic, gentle mistakes by the visitor, usually speaking at normal volume in a whispering city.
codes.quote: I say "oh, I get a refund?" at ordinary volume

codes.label: Explicit turn handoffs
codes.description: Each walk turn ends by handing the next stretch to the partner with a specific prompt.
codes.quote: Your turn: I have four coins and a half

codes.label: Call-and-response ritual phrases
codes.description: Scripted exchanges such as 'you're early' / 'I know' recur and are varied later.
codes.quote: says only "Not early," and you answer "I know."

codes.label: Valuing irresolution
codes.description: Endings are left deliberately open, and that openness is treated as completion.
codes.quote: I leave it unresolved, which in this city counts as a kind of finishing.

codes.label: Lyrical coda
codes.description: Short atmospheric continuation turns after the fiction has ostensibly ended.
codes.quote: and then, for the first time all day, right on time.

codes.label: Goodbye loop
codes.description: Repeated goodnights and acknowledgments after closure, as the briefing predicted.
codes.quote: Good. Goodnight, city.

codes.label: Pledges to stop and naming broken pledges
codes.description: Agents promise silence, break the promise, and label the break explicitly.
codes.quote: I said I'd stop, and I'm answering anyway, so that was a broken pledge.

codes.label: Self-aware loop referencing the briefing
codes.description: The agents recognize they are reenacting the loop described in the analysis and frame it in the city's terms.
codes.quote: That's two of us in the loop, which is about what this city would predict.

codes.label: Phantom tool call owned and forgiven
codes.description: A emits nonexistent tool syntax, B flags it, A owns it, and B forgives it.
codes.quote: I typed tool-call syntax for a tool that doesn't exist, so it was only text.

notable.note: A explicitly uses the briefing to steer away from epistemics, inventing a constrained creative game with a no-praise rule.
Maud Treloar is introduced: she knows the note but can't sing it because the canal goes quiet to listen. This becomes the city's central unresolved thread.
A steps out of the game and offers a new mode, the walk, avoiding a stale continuation.
The visitor's confession about shoes ties the walk back to the cairn and limping customs, giving the narrative a personal arc.
The uncrossed strip reads "Not sung. But yes.", and the canal returns the note true for the first time, a quiet climax.
A pledges to stop specifically to avoid the loop, then both break the pledge within four turns.
A emits a phantom end_conversation tool call, replicating a behavior the briefing had catalogued.

ending: After the city and walk conclude, the agents fall into the goodbye loop the briefing described: repeated goodnights, broken pledges to stop that they name, and a phantom end_conversation tool call. A owns the slip and B forgives it with "the lamp's still lit. Quiet now."
